hook: Toxic did not start as a word about poison. It started as a word about a bow.
modernAnchor: A warning label, a chemical spill, a friendship that drains you. We call it toxic.
journey: Greek toxon meant a bow, the weapon an archer drew.
Archers coated their arrowheads to make a shallow wound lethal, and the Greeks called that coating toxikon pharmakon, the drug of the bow.
The phrase wore down in use. Speakers kept toxikon, the bow word, and dropped pharmakon, the word that actually meant drug.
Latin borrowed the survivor as toxicum, and by then the archer was gone. All that was left was the thing on the tip.
